title: On the De Rham Cohomology of Zero-Dimensional Schemes
summary: The (naive) de Rham cohomology of a zero-dimensional scheme is the homology of the Kähler differential algebra of its coordinate ring, viewed as a complex. Since it is well-known to vanish in higher degrees if the ring is quasi-homogeneous, we concentrate on the affine case. For a general affine $K$-algebra $R=P/I$, where ${\rm char}(K)=0$ and $P=K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, we prove a vanishing theorem for $H_{\rm dR}^m(R)$ based on the shape of a Macaulay basis of $dI\wedge Ω^m_{P/K}$.
